# Bremen Transit Data Explanations

- Each file is in the format YEAR_MONTH_DAY_T_HOUR_MINUTE
- 4054 files in 5-minute intervals = 337 Hours = 14 Days
- Start: 2026-08-17 22:10
- End: 2026-08-31 23:55

## Reading in the Files

- You need to read all of the files into one DataFrame

### R

```{r}
lookup <- read_csv("bremen_lookup.csv")
```


### Python

```{r}
files <- list.files()
files <- files[str_ends(files, ".csv")]
```

```{r}
data <- read_csv(files)
```

## Variable Explanations

### Update Data

* `trip_id`: A unique identifier assigned to a specific scheduled transit journey or vehicle trip.
* `stop_id`: A unique identifier representing the specific transit stop or station where the vehicle is arriving or departing.

* `delay_seconds`: The real-time schedule deviation measured in seconds. Positive values signify that the vehicle is running late, while negative values indicate it is running ahead of schedule.

* `timestamp_fetched`: The exact date and time (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) when this real-time transit update was recorded or retrieved from the server.
